If your experience doesn’t align precisely with all the criteria, don't worry! We encourage you to still apply. Many people miss out on opportunities because they feel they don’t fit every requirement—we believe in attitude, growth and iteration, not perfection!


What we offer

  • Competitive salary and equity, reflecting your impact and ownership.
  • Purpose-driven mission: Build tools that help organisations act more sustainably and make the ESG data ecosystem more transparent.
  • Flexible hybrid setup: Berlin or London based candidates are strongly preferred, with access to our team and the wider startup community at the Merantix AI Campus.
  • Trust and autonomy: Own meaningful problems, shape the product, and influence how we build as the company grows.
  • A genuinely high-impact role: Increase our delivery capacity, strengthen the robustness of our platform, and accelerate product innovation.
  • Dynamic environment: Work in a small, ambitious team at the intersection of applied AI, enterprise software, and sustainability.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

Location

This is a full-time position based at our HQ in Munich or Cologne.

About the role

You solve the hard technical problems on live systems.

Once a customer is running on blp, their processes are business critical. Invoices post or they do not. Orders flow or they sit. Our support organisation resolves most of what comes in, and a lot of it is genuinely well handled by people early in their career. What is left is yours: the cases where the cause is not obvious, where it crosses systems, data and process logic at once, where the same symptom has three possible explanations and only one of them is right.

That is the job. Not a queue, and not the easy half of one. Everything difficult that comes out of the run phase lands with you.

Two things sit alongside the case work, and they are what make this a senior job rather than a harder version of a junior one.

Stabilising accounts
When an account's health goes bad, you go in and stabilise it. Not as a permanent assignment, but as a small, highly skilled squad that takes a customer whose numbers or whose confidence have slipped, works out what is actually wrong across the whole picture, fixes it, and hands back a customer who is running properly again. It is the most concentrated version of this work there is.

Taking effort out permanently
Anything that keeps arriving in the queue is a signal, and the answer is usually not more people answering it. It might be better self-service for customers, a customer-facing assistant that resolves the routine questions before they reach us, better diagnostics, or a change in how something is configured at deployment so the problem never occurs. You are expected to find those, make the case, and drive them through. That is how a support organisation scales without scaling headcount one for one, and it is value the customer feels directly.

You work across the boundary between what our platform does, what the customer's ERP does, and what their data actually looks like. You are the one who can read a failing case end to end and say what really happened, and then say credibly whether the fix is configuration, data, process, or a genuine product issue. When it is a product issue, you are the counterpart to our engineering and product teams: you bring the evidence, and because you have seen the same structural problem across several customers, your case is the one that moves the roadmap.

You are also how this function gets better rather than just bigger. The diagnostic tooling, the patterns, the documentation that lets a first-year person resolve what used to take a senior one: that is yours to build. And the interns and specialists coming through the team learn this craft from you.

You do not deliver integrations and you do not run go-lives. Our integrations engineers and technical project managers own that. You own what happens once it is live and it is challenging.

What you'll do

  • Own the technically difficult cases from our live customer base, end to end, to a verified root cause.

  • Diagnose across boundaries: platform behaviour, ERP behaviour, master data and process logic.

  • Decide what the real fix is, and make it: configuration, data, process, or a case for engineering.

  • Go into accounts with a deteriorating health score, diagnose across the whole picture, stabilise them and hand them back running properly.

  • Drive strategic initiatives that permanently reduce effort and improve the customer experience, from better diagnostics to customer-facing self-service and assistants.

  • Act as the counterpart to Product and Engineering, with evidence strong enough to change priorities.

  • Recognise structural problems across customers and push for them to be solved once.

  • Build the diagnostic tooling, patterns and documentation that raise what the rest of the team can resolve alone.

  • Mentor interns and earlier-career colleagues, and raise the technical bar of the function.

  • Support Consultants and Customer Success Managers on the technical substance of customer escalations.

What we're really looking for

The following key attributes ensure success in this role:

  • Root Cause, Not Symptom – You are not finished when it stops happening. You are finished when you know why.

  • Cross-Boundary Reasoning – You hold platform, ERP, data and process in your head at once and find where the truth is.

  • Credible Both Ways – You explain the same problem to an engineer and to a CFO, and both of them believe you.

  • Leverage – Your instinct is to remove the next hundred cases, not only to close this one. You would rather build the thing that makes a problem stop arriving.

  • Calm Under Escalation – When a business-critical process is stopped, you get more precise rather than faster.

  • Stabilizer Under Pressure: An unhappy client is not a fire to put out. It is a relationship to rebuild. You bring the temperature down, put structure back into the account, and align next steps so trust returns, not just silence

What you'll bring

  • Master's degree in a STEM field: computer science, engineering, information systems, mathematics, physics or similar. Strong candidates from a related field are welcome to make their case.

  • 3+ years in a technical customer-facing role: application support at depth, technical consulting, solution engineering, integration engineering or equivalent.

  • Demonstrable debugging ability across systems, not only within one. APIs, data mapping, interfaces, logs.

  • Comfortable with data. SQL or equivalent, and the instinct to check rather than assume.

  • German and English, both fluent. This is a hard requirement. Our customers work in German every day and our internal work runs in English.

  • Nice to have: ERP experience with SAP, Microsoft Dynamics or similar, scripting in any language, or exposure to workflow automation and process mining.

What you'll get

  • The hard problems, not the queue.

  • Influence on the product, with a direct line to Engineering and Product.

  • Room to shape the function, since the practice is still being built.

  • Real growth – the path from here leads into Consulting, technical leadership within Customer Success, or Product.

  • Employee ownership – be part of a majority employee-owned company with a best-in-class stock option programme.

  • Amazing team – become part of a driven and collaborative group of innovators.

  • Visits & offsites – including collaborative team offsites.

Ready to build the future of ERP automation? Join us and own your impact.

jobs.title: Customer Success Engineer (Internship)
jobs.description:
Customer Success Engineer (Internship)

Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

Location

This is a six-month internship based in Munich or Cologne. This is an in-person role. You learn this job by sitting next to people who already do it, and that does not work remotely.

About the role

Think of this role as the modern Sherlock Holmes — new puzzles to solve and new people to work with, every single day.
This role sits exactly at the intersection of technology and business, and that is not a figure of speech. On one side you are in the system, in the data, working out what actually happened. On the other you are on a call with a finance team explaining it and agreeing what to do. You need both, every day.

Our customers run their finance and supply chain processes on blp. When something does not behave the way they expected, a document that did not post, an exception that should have resolved itself, a number in a dashboard that looks wrong, they write to us. That is where your work starts, and it is also where you become the face of blp for that customer. What reaches them is you: your answer, your explanation, your judgement about what to do next.

You will not be reading from a script and escalating. You investigate what the system did, what the data says and what the customer's process actually requires. You have the access and the authority to change configuration when that is the answer. And when it is not, you know who to bring in and what to give them.

The role grows with you. You start on cases where the pattern is known and someone is close by. As your expertise builds you take the harder ones, and your exposure to customers grows with it: from written answers, to calls, to being in the room when a customer wants their most pressing problem solved now.

This goes well beyond tickets. We are a fast-moving organisation and a lot of what needs to exist does not exist yet. You will take on and drive initiatives that make the whole operation scale: a recurring problem that should be solved once rather than fifty times, a piece of tooling that does not exist, a way of working that has outgrown itself. Interns here have shipped things that the team still uses.

How we think about ownership
You will be given real work with real consequences, early, because that is the only way anyone learns this job properly. The other half of that is judgement: explore and decide for yourself where you can, and pull someone in when something critical is on the line. Knowing which situation you are in is part of the skill, and nobody will hold it against you for asking. What matters is that you are the face of blp to that customer, and that you take that seriously.

Most of our customers work in German and you will be in front of them from early on. That is uncomfortable for about three weeks and then it is the best part of the job.

This is a real internship, not an observation post. You will be trusted with live customers quickly, with people close by while you learn.

What you'll do

  • Answer incoming customer requests through our support channel, and be the person they hear back from.

  • Own incidents end to end: investigate, resolve, and confirm with the customer that it is actually fixed.

  • Work out why a workflow, document or posting did not behave as expected.

  • Adjust configuration where that is the right fix.

  • Recognise when a problem is bigger than one case, and hand it on with proper evidence.

  • Join customer calls to work through urgent issues directly, as your experience grows.

  • Take on initiatives beyond the queue: things that should be fixed once rather than answered repeatedly.

  • Document what you learn so the next person does not have to learn it twice.

What we're really looking for

We do not expect you to know ERP systems. We expect you to be the kind of person who gets to the bottom of things.

  • Curiosity – You want to know why something works, not just that it does.

  • Clear Logic – You take a messy situation apart, find the actual cause, and explain it simply.

  • Customer Nerve – You stay calm and credible with a frustrated controller on the phone, and you can say "I do not know yet, here is how I will find out."

  • Self-Driven – You close your own knowledge gaps without being told to.

  • Ownership – You see things through without someone checking, and you know when to pull someone in.

What you'll bring

  • Enrolled in or recently completed a Bachelor's or Master's in business, economics, information systems, engineering, computer science, or something adjacent. Strong candidates from other backgrounds are welcome to make their case.

  • German and English, both fluent. This is a hard requirement. Our customers work in German every day and our internal work runs in English.

  • Strong analytical thinking and comfort working with data.

  • Genuine interest in enterprise software, AI, and how large organisations actually run.

  • Nice to have, not required: first exposure to ERP systems, SQL, APIs, or process modelling.

Where it leads

Our internship is the main entry point into the delivery organisation. Interns who do well are offered a permanent role, most often as a Customer Success Engineer or as an AI Automation Specialist, and from there the paths into Consulting and into project management are well travelled. We tell you early and honestly whether that conversation is coming.

What you'll get

  • Real responsibility from week three, not shadowing.

  • A steep learning curve on live enterprise systems.

  • Direct access to engineers, product managers, and the people running our customers' finance operations.

  • Employee ownership – be part of a majority employee-owned company with a best-in-class stock option programme.

  • Amazing team – become part of a driven and collaborative group of innovators.

  • Visits & offsites – including collaborative team offsites.

Ready to build the future of ERP automation? Join us and own your impact.

Senior Frontend Engineer, Marketing Website

Synthesia is the world’s leading AI video platform for business, used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. Founded in 2017, the company is headquartered in London, with offices and teams across Europe and the US.

As AI continues to shape the way we live and work, Synthesia develops products to enhance visual communication and enterprise skill development, helping people work better and stay at the center of successful organizations.

Following our recent Series E funding round, where we raised $200 million, our valuation stands at $4 billion. Our total funding exceeds $530 million from premier investors including Accel, NVentures (Nvidia's VC arm), Kleiner Perkins, GV, and Evantic Capital, alongside the founders and operators of Stripe, Datadog, Miro, and Webflow.

About the role

As a Senior Frontend Engineer on our Website team, you'll be a co-owner of the platform behind synthesia.io: the component library, content model and rendering stack that every page on our marketing site is built from. You'll shape direction and make key technical decisions with the team, likely with a focus area of your own but context across the whole system. This is a hands-on engineering role, and your primary output is high-quality component and schema code, plus the tooling that lets others build with it.

Millions of people visit synthesia.io every month, and it is one of the main ways we win new customers. That comes with real responsibility. The decisions you make are seen at scale, and we set the quality bar accordingly.

The defining challenge of this role is composability: a marketing site that marketers, and increasingly AI agents, can build pages with, without breaking design, performance or SEO.

You can expect to:

  • Build, scale and evolve our section library: the Astro components, Sanity schemas and design tokens that let us compose marketing pages consistently and accessibly.

  • Own the content model. Design schemas that resist misuse, so an editor, or an agent, can build a page that is correct by construction rather than correct by review.

  • Take Figma component specs all the way to production: responsive across mobile, tablet and desktop, accessible by default, matching design intent precisely.

  • Extend the platform for AI-assisted development, so coding agents can generate on-brand, on-spec sections from a design spec as reliably as a person can.

  • Own SEO integrity as a first-class engineering concern: canonicals, sitemaps, structured data, redirects, and no traffic cliffs on launch.

  • Raise the bar on engineering standards across the website surface: thorough code review, patterns others can follow, and tests around the parts that actually break.

  • Maintain and extend localisation across nine locales and a translation pipeline, so the system works for a global audience.

  • Shape the technical direction of the website platform over the next 6 to 12 months, and champion its adoption with the people who publish on it.

What we're looking for

  • At least five (5) years as a software engineer, including three (3) at senior level, building front end for content-driven or marketing platforms.

  • Real ownership of a content model in Sanity. You've designed schemas other people had to live with, and you have opinions about references vs. embedded objects, when a variant belongs in the schema versus at runtime, and how to stop a section library sprawling. GROQ and Portable Text are familiar territory.

  • Deep front-end expertise: expert HTML, CSS and TypeScript, with a strong command of component API design and the developer experience of a shared library.

  • You can work end to end. Comfortable owning the server side as well as the front end: SSR, serverless and edge runtimes, API routes, a SQL database, secrets and CI. You should be able to take a feature from schema to component to the route that serves it without handing off, and be happy debugging something that only reproduces in production.

  • Solid understanding of responsive design, cross-browser compatibility and web performance, and comfortable building to WCAG 2.2 AA. Accessibility is part of your definition of done, not a separate pass.

  • You care that marketing sites are measured, on performance, SEO, analytics events and conversion, and you're happy being accountable to those numbers.

  • A strong sense of craft and attention to detail, and the judgement to balance design intent against engineering constraints.

  • Strong communication and collaboration skills. You explain your reasoning, review generously, and treat levelling up the people around you as part of the job.

Nice to haves

  • Prior experience working on a large SaaS marketing website, at real traffic and with real stakes attached.

  • Astro, or another islands or static-site framework.

  • Cloudflare Workers, or another edge or serverless platform.

  • Experience with AWS Lambda.

  • Tailwind CSS v4, and experience working from a token-based design system.

  • Experience, or strong interest, in making component libraries and content models consumable by AI agents.

  • A strong design sensibility: an eye for visual detail and the judgement to push back on and improve design decisions, not just build them.

  • Experience with localisation and internationalisation at scale for a global audience.

  • Analytics and tag management implementation: dataLayer events, server-side tagging, getting attribution right without hurting performance.

Our culture

At Synthesia we're passionate about building, not talking, planning or politicising. We strive to hire the smartest, kindest and most unrelenting people and let them do their best work without distractions. Our work principles serve as our charter for how we make decisions, give feedback and structure our work to empower everyone to go as fast as possible. You can find out more about these principles here.

The hiring process:

  • 30 min call with our Technical Recruiter

  • 45 min call with the Head of Website about your past projects

  • 75 min practical exercise with one of our engineers. We hand you a real Figma section spec and work through how you'd model and build it. Collaborative, not Leetcode.

  • 60 min call with leadership, focused on examples of collaboration, growth, and the details of your future team.

Other important info:

  • Our preference is for this role to be based either in-office or remote in London, UK. We can also accommodate remote workers elsewhere in Europe subject to compliance and right to work checks.

  • This is full-time employment only, usually through OysterHR. No contractors possible.

  • Regionalentwicklung & Kohäsionspolitik

  • Ausgeprägte redaktionelle und kommunikative Fähigkeiten sowie die Fähigkeit, komplexe Sachverhalte zielgruppengerecht, klar und ausgewogen aufzubereiten
  • Abgeschlossenes Studium in einem relevanten Fachgebiet, belastbare empirische Methodenkenntnisse; Selbständigkeit sowie eine analytische, verbindliche und teamorientierte Arbeitsweise
  • Bereitschaft zu gelegentlichen (z. T. auch internationalen) Dienstreisen; sehr gute Sprachkenntnisse in Deutsch und Englisch, weitere Sprachen von Vorteil

Senior Learning, Development and Culture Manager (m/f/d)

TYTAN Technologies

The PACE is fast. The expectations are high. The contribution matters. Working at TYTAN is more than a job, this is a mission. We thrive, think big, and hold ourselves to the highest standard. Our mission and values guide everything we do, and we're looking for people who thrive on ownership, embrace challenges, and are energized by meaningful work. If you're motivated by impact and thrive in dynamic environments, you'll fit right in.

At TYTAN, we aim to set a global standard in autonomous air defense with AI-driven, cost-efficient systems that counter unmanned aerial threats at scale. We protect people. We protect critical infrastructure. We protect Europe’s sovereignty.

We are looking for a Learning, Development and Culture Manager to lead initiatives that foster continuous learning, strengthen leadership capability, and cultivate an engaging, high-performance workplace culture. This role partners with different leads and the HR department to design and deliver learning programs, drive employee engagement, and embed our organizational values across the employee lifecycle.

Your Roadmap to make an Impact

Learning & Development

  • Develop and implement the company's learning and development strategy.

  • Identify capability gaps and create learning solutions aligned with business objectives.

  • Design, coordinate, and evaluate training programs, workshops, and e-learning initiatives.

  • Manage onboarding and orientation programs for new employees.

  • Support leadership development, career growth, and succession planning.

  • Track learning effectiveness through participation, feedback, and business impact metrics.

Culture & Employee Engagement

  • Lead initiatives that strengthen employee engagement and organizational culture.

  • Plan and execute employee engagement activities, recognition programs, and company events.

  • Partner with leaders to reinforce company values and promote a positive work environment.

  • Analyze employee feedback and recommend actions to improve the employee experience.

  • Support change management and culture transformation initiatives.

Business Partnership

  • Collaborate with department heads to understand development needs.

  • Manage external training providers and learning budgets.

  • Ensure compliance with mandatory training requirements.

  • Stay informed about learning trends and recommend innovative development practices.


  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Organizational Development, Psychology, or a related field.

  • Minimum 3 years of experience in Learning & Development, Talent Development, Organizational Development, or a similar role.

  • Proven experience developing and implementing learning strategies, training programs, and leadership development initiatives.

  • Strong project management skills with the ability to manage multiple initiatives and stakeholders.

  • Expertise in instructional design, adult learning methodologies, and creating engaging learning experiences.

  • Excellent communication, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence leaders and collaborate across functions.

  • Strong organizational skills, a proactive mindset, and the ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment.

  • Fluent in German and English, both written and spoken.

Why TYTAN?

  • Build technology with real operational impact: Develop autonomous defence systems designed to protect lives and strengthen Europe’s security

  • Shape scalable defence capabilities: Work on solutions built for mass deployment, cost efficiency, resilience, and reliable production at scale

  • Move fast and take ownership: Work in a focused, high-performance team where decisions are made quickly and individual contributions have immediate impact

  • Define a new generation of defence technology: Join early and help shape the products, engineering standards, culture, and direction of a fast-growing deep-tech company

  • Work with an international mission-driven team: Collaborate with experienced specialists united by the goal of creating sovereign and effective security capabilities for Europe

  • Regular health care events: Health check-ups, skin screenings, mental health workshops, and an annual vitamin infusion on us

  • Referral bonus: Earn a reward when someone you refer joins the team

  • Regular team events: On- and off-site activities to connect and celebrate together

  • Corporate discounts: Exclusive employee discounts across a wide range of partner brands

  • Flexibility: Flexible working hours and hybrid work model, plus a modern Munich office built for focus and collaboration

About us

At TYTAN, it is more than just a job; it is about embracing autonomy, personal growth, and purpose. Make a lasting impact in the new era of defense! Join us to create a safer world for all.

WE are an equal-opportunity employer committed to fairness and inclusivity. We do not prioritize any specific religion, gender, nationality, or background. Due to security clearance requirements, affiliations with countries listed under § 13 para. 1 no. 17 SÜG may affect the application process.

jobs.description:
Product Designer, Generative Media (Staff-Level / L6)

Synthesia is the world’s leading AI video platform for business, used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. Founded in 2017, the company is headquartered in London, with offices and teams across Europe and the US.

As AI continues to shape the way we live and work, Synthesia develops products to enhance visual communication and enterprise skill development, helping people work better and stay at the center of successful organizations.

Following our recent Series E funding round, where we raised $200 million, our valuation stands at $4 billion. Our total funding exceeds $530 million from premier investors including Accel, NVentures (Nvidia's VC arm), Kleiner Perkins, GV, and Evantic Capital, alongside the founders and operators of Stripe, Datadog, Miro, and Webflow.

Location: Europe remote or London hybrid

The role:

We're looking for a Staff (L6) Product Designer to lead design for Synthesia's AI Playground: our dedicated generative-media workspace where users experiment with leading AI models to create video clips, images, and motion graphics, then feed those assets into Synthesia Studio videos.

Playground sits at an intentional crossroad: it's both a creation destination in its own right and a strategic on-ramp that converts experiments into polished videos. The product is evolving rapidly - from a single-format surface into a multi-format creation hub (video, images, motion graphics) with Templates & Apps ahead.

You'll operate as a senior IC: setting direction, influencing roadmap decisions (not just contributing), shaping bets with Product and Engineering leaders and raising the craft bar on how generative tools actually feel.

In practice, this role is about solving generative-media design problems, for example:

  • Designing prompt experiences and iteration workflows that make complex AI capabilities feel accessible and powerful - giving users meaningful agency without overwhelming them.

  • Balancing discovery across multiple media formats so none feels buried, while scaling for Templates, Apps, and future workflows.

  • Designing the invisible handoff between Playground creation and Studio editing - so experiments flow naturally into polished videos.

  • Working at the frontier of how generative media changes what "creation" means, where the best patterns are genuinely still being invented.

In this role you will:

  • Own Playground's evolution end-to-end: from single-format surface to scalable multi-format creation hub.

  • Set design direction for discovery, experimentation, and iteration across all formats. Influence adjacent product areas (Studio, Media Library) to stay coherent.

  • Partner with Product and Engineering to define what "great" looks like (principles, quality bar, metrics) and drive toward it.

  • Prototype and test interaction models quickly. Know when high-fidelity matters versus learning through Lo-Fi.

  • Raise the bar on craft: prompt UX, format balance, iteration workflows, and the feel of creating with AI at speed.

You should apply if you bring:

  • Significant experience designing creation tools or generative-media platforms where users explore, iterate, and refine outputs quickly.

  • Strong craft in interaction and visual design. A track record of shipping delightful experiences around complex workflows.

  • Deep comfort designing around AI model constraints. You design UX that works with constraints, not around them.

  • Systems thinking. You can hold the tension between Playground as a destination and as an on-ramp to Studio.

  • Experience designing multi-format products. You know how to give equal weight to different experiences and scale beyond an initial, focused surface.

  • Excellent communication in design reviews and cross-functional tradeoffs between user delight and business goals.

  • A track record of tackling novel problems in fast-moving generative-media spaces and turning early-stage bets into scalable platforms.

  • The ability to leverage feedback from users and customers to ensure the product continues to meet real needs - from SMBs shipping quick marketing videos through to Enterprise teams producing at scale.

At Synthesia we expect everyone to:

  • Put the Customer First

  • Own it & Go Direct

  • Be Fast & Experimental

  • Make the Journey Fun

You can read more about this in this public Notion page: https://synthesia.notion.site/How-we-work-at-Synthesia-f794caa72f8446efb6be22b551ce0fa2

Benefits

  • A flexible, remote friendly role based out of Europe or one of our hubs in London, Copenhagen, Munich, or Zurich.

  • 25 days of annual leave + public holidays in the country where you are based.

  • A generous referral scheme.

  • Work from home set up.

  • At Synthesia, you can work from anywhere (within reason) in the world for up to 60 days per year!

  • A huge opportunity for career growth as you’ll help shape a market-defining product.

jobs.title: Senior Regional Marketing Manager
Inbound Sales 🇫🇷
jobs.description:
Inbound Sales 🇫🇷

Health can’t wait.

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

⚡ The Inbound Sales 🇫🇷 role

We're growing our Inbound Sales team in France.

Our Inbound Sales team is in charge of closing inbound requests from leads with 1 to 5 employees (Independent workers, very small companies, individuals).

You’ll be in charge of the whole sales cycle from qualification to closing by educating prospects and providing inspiring arguments to transform them into convinced customers.

At the same time, we expect you to understand, embrace and apply the Alan Smart & Soft selling method. This method stems from the concept that the prospect experience is an inseparable piece of the overall Alan customer experience. You are expected to make this experience pleasant, instructive and delightful by leveraging the most relevant messaging and materials (Smart) and by defining the high-touch strategy that suits best each prospect (Soft).

We also expect you to look at the big picture and help us grow and improve as a company. For that, you’ll have to be real team players even beyond your role. You’ll be expected to challenge us to improve our product(s), our methods, and our strategy, and get involved in other projects and initiatives relevant to growing our customer base.

What does make this role exciting :

  • You will close deals every single day of the year, which is very stimulating!

  • The Inbound Sales team is quite recent: You will contribute to building a new practice within the Sales Community, getting involved in tooling and process improvements

  • You will help building the playbook of best practices to close deals in one shot

  • You will contribute to making our products even better by sharing feedback and improving the self-serve experience for our members

  • You will become an insurance expert and learn to master our products in order to confidently answer questions & objections from prospects

  • We invest heavily in AI to transform the Sales practice. You'll have the opportunity to become one of the most modern Sales professionals in the market!

⭐ You will be a great fit for this role if you: 

  • Have 1-2 years of experience in a Sales role including closing experience

  • Have full working proficiency in French (C2 and above), and advanced level in English

  • Are highly organized with exceptional follow-up skills

  • Show a great balance between Active Listening and Assertiveness when interacting with your prospects

  • Have natural empathy and are passionate about understanding and solving prospects' problems

  • Have a positive attitude and ability to collaborate in a small team

  • Have a desire to learn fast and make an impact from day 1

  • Are based in (or willing to relocate to) Paris, Bordeaux, Marseille, Lyon, Annecy, Nantes or Biarritz.

For this opportunity, we are aiming to hire within the A2-B1 level range.

Everything else is a plus. We care about having a diversity of experiences, profiles and backgrounds in our team.

🙌   Perks & Benefits

At Alan, we believe that being in good health is a basic need, and it starts with our employees. This is why Alaners are provided with a stimulating environment and perks ensuring they are happy, efficient and spend only high-quality time with co-workers. 

Therefore, we offer:

  • Fair rewards. Generous equity packages complement your base salary, for permanent contracts only.

  • Flexible office with hybrid setup. Amazing office space at our Paris HQ or sponsored co-working hubs in Bordeaux, Marseille, Lyon, Annecy, Nantes or Biarritz.

  • All the tools you need. Top of the range equipment: Macbook Air, keyboard, laptop stand, monitor, and Bose noise-canceling headphones.

  • Flexible vacation policy and flexible working hours. Organize your time as you wish.

  • Delightful healthcare insurance: Extremely comprehensive health insurance - 100% for you and your children, 90-100% for partners depending on your country (permanent contracts only).

  • Transport. Generous transit benefit

  • Learning & Training opportunities. A highly flexible training policy free books and budget to attend and speak at conferences if the opportunity arises.

  • Personal growth through coaching: At Alan, coaching isn't just a perk - it's core to who we are. Every Alaner is paired with a dedicated coach from day one, who helps maximize their impact, nurture engagement, and navigate Alan's values to develop their full potential. Learn more about our coaching culture.

  • Parental leave. Extended parental leave for all new parents, for permanent contracts only.

Important note: we hire people not roles. 

After reading this job description, if you feel like you don’t have all the necessary prerequisites but that it matches where you are now or what you'd like to grow into in your next position, we encourage you to apply!

Not everybody will enter our recruitment process, but all, no matter how underrepresented, should feel free to apply as it can only bring learnings or success.

🔖 Check out our About Alan and Career pages, as well as our Medium, blog and Glassdoor page for more info.

Enterprise Account Executive - Munich (m/w/d)

Get to know us

Ideals is a global B2B SaaS product company recognized as the most highly rated and customer-centric brand in the secure business collaboration market. Trusted by over 2,000,000 users from 300,000 companies globally, we help people run high-stakes processes and make important decisions with less stress, higher quality, and shorter hours.

Ideals Virtual Data Room (VDR): Secure document sharing and collaboration for due diligence, fundraising, corporate reporting, licensing, clinical trials, and other complex transactions.

After 18 years in the market, we grow sustainably at 30%+ YoY and are now scaling 5x globally to disrupt the VDR category and reach unicorn status by 2029.

 

The role

Ideals has been in the Virtual Data Room space since 2008 and has built a trusted reputation with clients across multiple industries in Europe, including Orcan Energy, E-Gruppe, Deloitte, and EY.

To support the rapid expansion of the Ideals VDR line of business in Germany, we are looking for an Enterprise Account Executive (Key Accounts) in Munich to focus on our Corporate segment. Unlike our advisory-focused motions, you will sell directly to a wide variety of enterprise corporations across diverse industries (such as energy, pharma, biotech, and telecommunications).

As a quota-carrying strategic seller, your primary goal will be to grow sales and revenue through the acquisition of new strategic enterprise accounts and the expansion of existing ones. You will act as an impactful industry expert, generating demand, navigating complex 6 to 9-month sales cycles, and displacing incumbents by utilizing deep discovery and consultative selling frameworks.

Compensation package: 50% base salary; 50% performance-based variable.

Why Ideals?

  • Market-leading position: 18+ years in the VDR business, powering 10%+ of global M&A activity, with a 31% CAGR against competitors' 11%.

  • Mature high-trust sales org: Ideals ranks in the top 10% of over 15,000 sales organizations on RepVue, as rated by sales professionals. Expect strong Sales Enablement, RevOps, Marketing support, and a structured onboarding ramp.

  • Real growth trajectory: Profitable and bootstrapped, with 5x revenue growth and unicorn status targeted in the next five years, and real headroom to build the team.

 

What you will do

  • Proactively build and manage a pipeline focused on the acquisition of new strategic enterprise accounts (new logos)

  • Conduct solution-based sales engagements, including client meetings, executive presentations, and product demonstrations (face-to-face and virtual)

  • Maintain "White Space" analysis and execute strategic initiatives to upsell and cross-sell within the existing customer base

  • Develop and deliver comprehensive business cases that quantify the cost of inaction and address customer priorities, pain points, and ROI

  • Structure, negotiate, and close complex deals, guiding corporate clients step-by-step through enterprise procurement, security compliance, and legal processes

  • Orchestrate multi-threading strategies to navigate enterprise politics, establishing strong relationships with C-Suite executives and key stakeholders across various verticals

  • Keep an accurate track record of personal sales activities in the CRM, including methodical mid- and long-term forecasting

  • Provide relevant customer feedback to the product development team and collaborate with Customer Success, Marketing, and Inbound Sales to maximize revenue and customer satisfaction

What you bring

  • 4–7 years of demonstrable quota-carrying success in B2B sales

  • Proven track record of managing lengthy or complex enterprise sales cycles

  • Significant experience selling directly to C-level executives (CxOs) and multi-threading within large enterprise organizations

  • Clear understanding of, and practical experience with, consultative sales methodologies (e.g., MEDDIC/MEDPIC, SPIN, Challenger)

  • 4-year university degree (bachelor's)

  • Exceptional business communication skills, enabling you to execute executive storytelling, challenge the status quo, and handle complex contracting negotiations

  • High learning agility, analytical thinking, and commercial curiosity to quickly grasp the nuances of various corporate industries

  • High AI fluency and advanced CRM tracking skills

  • Native-level proficiency in German with professional English level (C1+)

 

Nice to have

  • Fluency in an additional language

  • Background in SaaS, financial technology, or information security sectors

  • Familiarity with enterprise M&A use cases and corporate compliance workflows

 

What we offer

We highly value our people, so we will empower you with all the resources and support to help you reach your full potential.

 

For your best work

  • Hybrid flexibility to shape your ideal workday

  • Home workplace budget

  • Co-working expense coverage

  • Individual IT budget for extra equipment

  • Top-tier tech and AI-powered tools

 

For your growth

  • Access to Ideals Academy with numerous courses

  • Investment in external learning and development activities

  • Guidance in Personal Development Plan creation

  • Professional literature and subscriptions coverage

  • Support of your passion as a speaker or writer

  • Internal talent mobility opportunities

 

For your well-being

  • Tailored Wellness Package to support your physical and mental health

  • Urban Sports membership

  • Funding for sports competitions

  • 30 business days of paid time off per year

  • Paid health-related time off

     

Extra perks

  • Budget for meetups with your local team

  • Generous internal referral program

 

Our culture

Commitment, Excellence, Collaboration, Trust and Care are core values to the Ideals team. For us, these are the principles that every Idealer lives and breathes. We are on the lookout for like-minded individuals who share our values. By doing so, we create a team where talents feel at ease and work to the best of their abilities.

Discover more

 

Ideals is an equal opportunity employer

At Ideals, we value a diverse, inclusive workforce and we provide equal employment opportunity for all applicants and employees. All qualified applicants for employment will be considered without regard to an individual’s race, color, sex, gender identity, gender expression, religion, age, national origin or ancestry, citizenship, physical disability, medical condition, family care status, marital status, domestic partner status, sexual orientation, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other basis protected by federal, state or local laws. jobs.title: Senior iOS Developer - Berlin
jobs.description:
Senior iOS Developer - Berlin

About RA

Resident Advisor has been a home for electronic music culture since 2001. Event discovery, ticketing, news and long-form editorial, artist profiles, original films, and a weekly mix series two decades deep. Around 7 million people use the web platform every month, with a wider audience across our apps and other channels. Underneath the platform sits a network of contributors and city managers across dozens of cities, which is how we stay connected to the scenes we cover rather than reporting on them from a distance. RA is 25 years old, independent, B.Corp certified and intent on being indispensable to the artists, promoters and audiences who make this culture.

The role

You'll be a senior engineer on the RA Guide iOS app: shaping how it's built, leading the technical design of larger features, and raising the bar on quality with the Apps lead.

RA Guide is RA's app for browsing events and buying tickets, native on iOS and Android and used by thousands of people every day. We also make RA Scan, a cross-platform app promoters use to scan tickets at the door. You'll join the Apps team: the Apps lead (who also builds on iOS), an Android developer and a product manager, working closely with design and the web teams who build the APIs the app uses.

We release weekly. Native releases can't be rolled back once they're out, so we care about getting each one right: tests, careful review, and watching what happens after release.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the technical design of larger features, including the specs that line up iOS and Android on the same APIs
  • Own areas of the codebase, and modernise older parts of it safely
  • Raise release quality: automated UI tests on native frameworks, crash analysis and monitoring
  • Review code and mentor other developers
  • Work with the web and platform teams on the APIs the app depends on
  • Help shape how the team uses AI in development, and where it shouldn't.

Who we are looking for

  • Several years building and releasing iOS apps used at scale
  • Deep experience with Swift, app architecture and refactoring code that's already live
  • Testing and coding habits for stable app releases
  • You make the developers around you better, through review, pairing and clear explanation
  • You can explain a technical trade-off to product and design in plain terms

If you meet most of these but not all, we'd still like to hear from you. We'll help you grow into the rest.

Nice to have

  • SwiftUI, reactive programming and GraphQL
  • A/B testing, phased rollouts and data tracking
  • Monitoring tools such as Datadog
  • Android or cross-platform experience
  • An interest in electronic music and the scenes RA serves

What we offer you

  • Generous annual leave policies aimed at promoting work-life balance.
  • Matched pension, or 401k for US staff.
  • Comprehensive staff wellbeing initiatives, featuring regular activities and workplace programmes to support mental and physical health. This includes discounted ClassPass memberships and custom-fitted earplugs.
  • Company-led social events, team lunches, and discounts on merch.
  • Paid annual volunteering allowance, encouraging contributions to community projects and charities you care about.
  • A transparent internal company culture committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion (see: https://ra.co/about/diversity).
  • Active involvement in community projects within the electronic music community (see: https://ra.co/about/community).

More about RA

We are independent and we intend to stay that way. 25 years in, RA answers to the culture it came from rather than to outside stakeholders. That is what enables us to make decisions on a long-term basis.

Our staff, contributors and international teams are not observers. They are part of the scenes we cover, and that is what we hire for. Craft first, and then a genuine stake in this music rather than just a job in it.

RA has been B Corp certified since 2024, which holds us to standards on social and environmental impact we would want to meet regardless of the badge.

We especially welcome applicants from diverse backgrounds, abilities, ethnicities, experiences, gender identities, and sexual orientations.

Our values

  • Electronic music is art.
  • We celebrate the progressive values that underpin electronic music.
  • We advocate for a more inclusive and equitable electronic music community.
  • We honour the past, present and future of electronic music.
  • We use innovation to empower the community.
  • We choose honesty over gain and purpose over profit.
  • We're always front left.

This role is a full-time based in our Berlin office. Please note: this position requires applicants to be based in Berlin and to work from the office three days per week. The annual salary range for this role is €70,000- €85,000. If you have questions about the role, please contact

jobs.description:
Post-doctorat en sociologie, ergonomie ou en sciences de gestion

1-    ENVIRONNEMENT DU POSTE

Grande école d’ingénieur généraliste de l’IMT-Institut Mines-Télécom, premier groupe d’écoles d’ingénieurs de France, IMT Atlantique a pour ambition d’accompagner les transitions, de former des ingénieurs responsables et mettre l'excellence scientifique et technique au service de l'enseignement, de la recherche et de l'innovation.

Le poste est rattaché au Département interdisciplinaire en sciences sociales (DI2S) rassemblant des enseignants chercheurs et enseignantes chercheuses en sciences de gestion, sociologie, économie et droit. Sur le campus de Nantes, les recherches sont focalisées sur l’analyse des transformations des organisations et des métiers dans des systèmes sociotechniques. Trois domaines d’investigation sont privilégiés : l’industrie, la santé et l’environnement. Le ou la candidate sera affilé·e au LEMNA (Laboratoire Économie et Management Nantes Atlantique).

Plus précisément, le poste sera rattaché à la chaire RESOH [Recherche en Sécurité Organisations Hommes]. Les travaux de recherche, à l’interface de la sociologie et de la gestion, portent sur le fonctionnement des organisations à hauts risques. Partant de l’analyse du travail et des organisations de travail, il s’agit d’éclairer les dimensions socio-organisationnelles, managériales et institutionnelles contribuant à (ou empêchant) le maintien d’un niveau de fiabilité compatible avec les exigences de sécurité et de production. Les recherches de la chaire sont conduites en étroite collaboration avec des partenaires industriels et institutionnels. Elles visent à produire des connaissances scientifiques, mais également à favoriser leur mise en discussion, leur appropriation et leur mobilisation par les acteurs concernés.

 

MISSIONS

En collaboration avec l’ensemble des enseignants-chercheurs de l’équipe (permanents et associés), les missions sont :

1-    Participer à l’enquête empirique et à la production scientifique

2-    Contribuer à la réflexion collective

3-    Participer aux réunions de coordination et aux réunions de restitution

4-    Diffuser et valoriser les connaissances et résultats produits

 ACTIVITÉS :

  1. Participer à l’enquête empirique et à la production scientifique

    • Réalise un travail bibliographique sur les thèmes de la chaire ?

    • Participe à l’élaboration du protocole d’enquête (notamment en étant force de proposition pour la sélection des sites et des activités étudiés, les grilles d’entretien et / ou d’observation)

    • Réalise une partie de l’analyse documentaire sur les secteurs industriels à risques (nucléaire, pétrochimie)

    • Participe à la collecte des données au sein des organisations partenaires en mobilisant des méthodologies qualitatives :

      • mène des entretiens semi-directifs avec des personnels (dirigeants, managers, ingénieurs, techniciens, opérateurs) ;

      • pratique des observations directes non participantes de séquence de travail au sein des sites identifiés ;

      • rédige des carnets d’observation ou tout autre document permettant le partage des observations ;

      • prépare et participe éventuellement à des focus groupes.

    • Prend part à la retranscription et au dépouillement des entretiens, aux traitements (manuel et/ou assisté par un logiciel d’analyse) et à l’analyse les données

    • Contribue à l’analyse des restitutions intermédiaires réalisées par l’équipe avec les personnels concerné.

  2. Contribuer à la réflexion collective de l’équipe

    • Contribue activement aux réunions à visée scientifique de l’équipe et aux séminaires de recherche de la chaire (au sein de l’équipe RESOH et avec les partenaires)

  3. Participer aux réunions de coordination de l'équipe et aux restitutions avec les organisations partenaires (au national, et en local en fonction des terrains)

    • Prépare des supports de restitution

    • Participe aux discussions d’équipe

    • Rédige des comptes rendus des restitutions aux enquêtés

  4. Diffuser et valoriser les connaissances et résultats produits

    • Rédige des communications pour des conférences nationales et/ou internationales

    • Contribue à l’organisation et participe aux manifestations scientifiques organisées par l’équipe (exemple : journée d’étude)

    • Participe à l’écriture d’articles à visée scientifique et de vulgarisation


Niveau de formation et/ou expérience minimums requis :

  • Doctorat obtenu moins de 3 ans avant la date d’embauche en sociologie, sciences de gestion ou ergonomie

Compétences, connaissances et expériences indispensables :

  • Bien connaître un ou plusieurs domaines d’expertise parmi les suivants : travail, organisation, outil de gestion, STS, ressources humaines

  • Maîtriser les approches qualitatives, avoir déjà réalisé une ou plusieurs étude(s) de cas (entretien semi-directif, observation non participante, focus group),

  • Avoir une très bonne maîtrise du français pour la réalisation des entretiens lors des enquêtes de terrain avec les membres des organisations partenaires

  • Témoigner d’une expérience de recherche pertinente pour le présent projet, et d’une ouverture aux collaborations académiques interdisciplinaires

Compétences, connaissances et expériences souhaitables (Facultatif) :

  • L’équipe étudiera avec attention les candidatures faisant état d’une connaissance de la littérature sur les organisations à hauts risques, la fiabilité ou résilience organisationnelle et les approches socio-techniques

  • Une appétence et une connaissance du monde de l’industrie seront appréciés.

  • Savoir utiliser des outils d’analyse qualitative (tels que Nvivo) et de bibliographie (tels que Zotero)

Capacités et aptitudes :

  • Qualités rédactionnelles

  • Sens de l’organisation

  • Autonomie dans la conduite de l’enquête de terrain

  • Capacité à travailler en équipe de recherche interdisciplinaire et multisite

  • Appétence pour les questions techniques, le projet étant résolument orienté vers des mondes industriels où la technique a une place importante. La personne recrutée travaillera prioritairement avec l’équipe de chercheur·euse·s en sociologie et sciences de gestion, mais aussi en interaction forte avec des ingénieurs et techniciens

  • Niveau d’anglais suffisant pour s’approprier la littérature scientifique anglo-saxonne

POURQUOI NOUS REJOINDRE :

👉 Un cadre de recherche d'excellence : Intégrez IMT Atlantique, première école d’ingénieurs de France, et contribuez aux travaux innovants de la chaire RESOH sur les organisations à hauts risques, en collaboration avec des partenaires industriels et institutionnels.

👉 Un défis intellectuels stimulants : Participez à des enquêtes empiriques, analysez des données qualitatives et contribuez à la production scientifique dans un cadre interdisciplinaire alliant sociologie, gestion et ergonomie.

👉 Un impact concret sur la société : Valorisez les résultats de recherche en les rendant accessibles aux acteurs socio-économiques, et influencez les pratiques organisationnelles dans des secteurs clés comme l’industrie, la santé et l’environnement.

LE PLUS :

jobs.description:
Doctorant(e) - "Vers un bâtiment low-tech : caractériser et réduire les dépendances liées à la maintenance et à l'entretien du bâti face au changement climatique"

Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain.

Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.

L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.

Transitions numériques, écologiques, industrielles : les grands défis de notre époque sont aussi ceux de l’Institut Henri Fayol.

Ici se mêlent Informatique, Sciences des données, Management, Sciences humaines et sociales, Génie environnemental pour penser les systèmes complexes de demain : territoires, entreprises, filières industrielles. 

📊 Résilience, performance, durabilité… Nous développons et expérimentons en lien étroit avec les acteurs socio-économique pour répondre aux exigences des transitions actuelles.

✨ Une recherche interdisciplinaire à fort impact, où l’humain est toujours au centre. 

Cette thèse de doctorat sera rattachée au département Génie de l'Environnement pour les Organisations (GEO), membre du Laboratoire CNRS UMR 5600 Environnement Ville et Société (EVS). Pour répondre aux enjeux des transitions écologique, énergétique et industrielle, le département GEO accompagne les acteurs des territoires (acteurs publics et privés) vers une meilleure prise en compte des enjeux environnementaux et de résilience territoriale. Il s'attache ainsi à apporter des solutions nouvelles en matière d'analyse, de modélisation et d'évaluation environnementale des systèmes industriels et territoriaux dans un double contexte d'industrie des futurs et de villes et territoires soutenables.

🏠 Contexte

Présentation du sujet

Le changement climatique met en lumière, comme l'a fait auparavant la crise COVID, les vulnérabilités et liens de dépendance généralisée de nos modes de vie envers les infrastructures, les chaînes de valeur, et modes d'organisation économique et technique, éléments souvent déconnectés de l'usager final, de ses besoins et des conditions d'occupation. Pour le secteur du bâtiment, Cimerman (2023) évoque une tendance depuis plusieurs décennies de « simplification cartésienne » de la conception et de l'opération du bâti. Celle-ci se traduit notamment par le développement d'un imaginaire de « bâtiment-machine », se traduisant par une superposition d'éléments techniques complexes (chauffage, ventilation, climatisation), susceptibles d'être pilotés au travers d'outils informatiques et d'une gestion centralisée optimisée (Cimerman, 2023).

Face aux enjeux posés par le changement climatique, deux voies opposées d'adaptation du bâti se dessinent. La première, actuellement dominante, consiste à prolonger cet imaginaire de « bâtiment-machine », rationalisable, mesurable et optimisable, et ce notamment au travers du développement du « smart-building ». Cette approche technosolutionniste apporte des réponses clés-en-main (capteurs, outils de pilotage centralisés, etc.) aux gestionnaires et usagers de bâtiments. Néanmoins, elle présente certains défis pour leur maintenance et leur entretien. Nous pouvons citer le recours massif aux nouvelles technologies, coûteuses, complexes, rapidement obsolètes et dont la fabrication repose en grande partie sur des ressources finies. Cela pose de plus les questions centrales des compétences, de la délégation du savoir et des outils associés à des opérateurs experts externes.

En contrepoint à la première voie, une seconde approche, encore marginale, émerge : celle d'un « bâtiment low-tech ». Popularisée ces dernières années en France par Philippe Bihouix (Bihouix, 2014), la low-tech questionne le rapport à la technologie et aux différentes formes de dépendances qu'elle génère (Tanguy et al., 2023). Dans le secteur du bâtiment, l'application de cette démarche renvoie souvent à la dépendance à la ressource (énergie et matière) : repenser les usages, l'origine des matériaux (réemployés, biosourcés) ou encore la simplicité de l'équipement utilisé. Bien que nécessaires, ces travaux s'intéressent pourtant peu à d'autres formes de dépendances associées à la technique, au titre desquelles nous pouvons citer la dépendance aux savoirs et aux formes d'organisation sociale et économique qui conditionnent l'adéquation, la pérennité et l'efficacité des solutions proposées.

Cette thèse offre ainsi une immersion concrète dans les questions d'adaptation du parc bâti au changement climatique par la « lowtech » à l'interface entre sciences de l'ingénieur et sciences humaines et sociales. Les compétences et l'expérience acquises trouveront une résonance particulière dans un secteur en pleine mutation, où la maîtrise des dépendances techniques, économiques et organisationnelles devient un enjeu central pour la soutenabilité des bâtiments et de leur exploitation.

Contexte scientifique

La littérature consacrée à la low-tech s'est structurée ces dernières années autour d'une critique de la fuite en avant technologique et des dépendances qu'elle engendre (Bihouix, 2014 ; Tanguy et al., 2023). Appliquée au bâtiment, cette littérature reste toutefois majoritairement centrée sur la phase de conception et sur la dépendance à la ressource : sobriété énergétique, choix de matériaux biosourcés ou réemployés, réduction du niveau d'équipement technique.

Deux angles morts en découlent. Le premier concerne la phase d'exploitation : la maintenance et l'entretien, qui représentent pourtant l'essentiel de la durée de vie d'un bâtiment et conditionnent la performance réelle des solutions installées, sont peu traités comme objet de recherche à part entière. Le second concerne la nature même des dépendances étudiées. Au-delà de la ressource, la conduite d'une opération de maintenance mobilise des savoirs et savoir-faire, des outils de diagnostic, des pièces détachées, des prestataires et des chaînes d'approvisionnement, ainsi que des cadres contractuels et réglementaires. Ces dépendances d’ordres cognitives, organisationnelles, économiques restent largement implicites et sous développées dans les travaux existants.

La caractérisation de ces dépendances soulève par ailleurs une question d'échelle. Analysée au seul niveau du bâtiment, la maintenance apparaît comme une somme d'opérations techniques ; replacée à l'échelle urbaine, elle révèle des réseaux d'acteurs, des filières, des compétences localement disponibles ou absentes, et des effets de dépendance mutualisés.

Contexte opérationnel

Du côté des acteurs institutionnels et économiques, de nombreux outils accompagnent aujourd'hui la gestion technique du patrimoine bâti. Nous pouvons citer :

  • les outils de gestion de maintenance assistée par ordinateur (GMAO) et les plateformes de gestion technique du bâtiment (GTB) ;

  • les démarches de modélisation des données du bâtiment (BIM d'exploitation, jumeaux numériques) et les labels associés à la connectivité des bâtiments ;

  • les contrats d'exploitation et de maintenance externalisés, et les dispositifs de garantie de performance énergétique ;

  • les démarches et retours d'expérience issus de la mouvance low-tech (chantiers démonstrateurs, guides praticiens, réseaux associatifs).

Ces dispositifs partagent une orientation commune : ils visent à optimiser la conduite de la maintenance, rarement à interroger les dépendances qu'elle installe. Les démarches low-tech, à l'inverse, portent cette interrogation mais restent au stade de l'expérimentation ponctuelle, sans cadre d'évaluation partagé ni capacité de généralisation à l'échelle d'un parc ou d'un territoire.

Il en résulte, en l'état des connaissances aussi bien scientifiques qu'opérationnelles, qu'il n'existe pas de méthode permettant de rendre visibles et de qualifier les dépendances associées à la maintenance et à l'entretien des bâtiments, ni d'évaluer dans quelle mesure une approche low-tech permettrait de les réduire.


🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous

Démarche de la thèse

L'objectif principal de cette thèse est de caractériser les apports d'une approche low-tech pour cartographier et maîtriser, sinon réduire, les différentes formes de dépendances associées à la maintenance et à l'entretien des bâtiments.

Les dépendances analysées s'appuieront sur les techniques, pratiques, outils et réseaux en lien avec la maintenance qui seront mis en évidence dans les deux autres thèses du projet PERENNIS. Cette thèse s'inscrit donc en complète continuité de ces deux travaux.

Dans un premier temps, il s'agira de construire un cadre d'analyse des dépendances liées à la maintenance du bâtiment, articulant quatre registres : les ressources (énergie, matière, pièces détachées), les savoirs et savoir-faire, les acteurs et leurs relations contractuelles, et les réseaux techniques et logistiques. Cette phase s'appuiera sur une revue de la littérature scientifique et « grise », sur un benchmark des pratiques et outils de maintenance existants, et sur des entretiens avec les acteurs du secteur (gestionnaires de patrimoine, bailleurs, mainteneurs, bureaux d'études, collectivités).

Dans un deuxième temps, ce cadre sera mobilisé pour caractériser et rendre visibles les schémas de dépendance à l'échelle urbaine, sur un ou plusieurs territoires d'étude. Il s'agira notamment d'identifier les sources de données mobilisables pour objectiver ces schémas, de qualifier les points de fragilité et d'apprécier leur variabilité selon les typologies de bâtiments et les configurations d'acteurs.

Dans un troisième temps, des stratégies prospectives low-tech de maintenance et d'entretien seront proposées et instruites. Il s'agira de construire des scénarios contrastés, d'évaluer leur capacité à réduire la vulnérabilité technique, économique et sociale des opérations de maintenance dans un contexte d'adaptation au changement climatique, et d'en discuter la faisabilité et l'acceptabilité avec les parties prenantes concernées.

Verrous scientifiques :

  • Définition et opérationnalisation de la notion de dépendance appliquée à la maintenance du bâti, au-delà de la seule dépendance à la ressource (savoirs, acteurs, organisations, réseaux)

  • Caractérisation et représentation de schémas de dépendance à l'échelle urbaine, à partir de données hétérogènes et partiellement indisponibles

  • Évaluation prospective de stratégies low-tech en l'absence de retours d'expérience consolidés et de métriques établies

  • Articulation interdisciplinaire entre sciences de l'ingénieur et sciences humaines et sociales, et capacité à répliquer l'approche tout en visant la « parcimonie » des méthodes et modèles

Objectifs de développement durable rattachés :

ODD 11 – Villes et communautés durables ·

ODD 12 – Consommation et production responsables

ODD 13 – Mesures relatives à la lutte contre les changements climatiques.


🔍 Ce que nous recherchons

Formation : Bac +5 en ingénierie généraliste, sciences de l'environnement, génie civil ou énergétique du bâtiment, géographie/aménagement, ou discipline connexe. Une formation ou une sensibilité aux sciences humaines et sociales (sociologie des techniques, STS, économie de la fonctionnalité) serait un plus.

Compétences requises :

  • Méthodes qualitatives : conduite et analyse d'entretiens semi-directifs, observation de terrain, analyse de corpus documentaires.

  • Analyse systémique et prospective : capacité à représenter un système sociotechnique, à construire et instruire des scénarios.

  • Connaissance du bâtiment : compréhension du fonctionnement technique du bâti et de ses équipements, et des logiques d'exploitation et de maintenance.

  • Traitement de données : aisance avec des données hétérogènes issues de sources variées ; la maîtrise d'outils de traitement (R, Python) ou de SIG (QGIS) serait appréciée.

  • Gestion de projets : aptitude à structurer et mener des phases de projet de manière autonome, en articulation avec deux autres doctorants du projet.

Langue : français courant et anglais opérationnel (capacité à lire des publications techniques et scientifiques en anglais).

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Overview

Harmattan AI is developing new hardware products within the Launcher module: field-deployable drone launchers designed to be deployed and operated autonomously in demanding field environments. These products require dedicated electronics design with complex architecture in a constrained environment – PCBs integrating power conversion, energy management, control and communication interfaces – optimised for cost at volume. The Launcher team is seeking a dedicated hardware engineer to own electronics design end-to-end and accelerate the path to production milestones.

Ideal candidate

A senior hardware engineer who has designed and shipped complex PCBs, ideally mixing digital and significant power (hundreds of watts), into production. They are rigorous on schematics, layout, and bring-up, and have a strong instinct for cost and manufacturability. They design with real-world operating conditions in mind - temperature, moisture, surges - and an interest in battery thermal management; direct experience of outdoor-deployed equipment is a plus rather than a prerequisite. They are comfortable working autonomously in a small team and can bridge hardware and firmware.

Skills required

  • PCB schematic and layout design (Altium Designer preferred)

  • Power electronics design: ~300 W DC/DC conversion, protection, derating, efficiency and thermal budgets

  • Thermal regulation: temperature sensing and control loops, battery storage temperature management, heatsinking

  • Power over Ethernet (IEEE 802.3af/at/bt): combined power and data delivery, isolation, cable budgets

  • Mixed-signal design: power management, MCU interfaces, communication buses (SPI, I2C, UART, USB, CAN, Ethernet)

  • Hardware bring-up and debug: bench equipment proficiency

  • DFM/DFA for PCB manufacturing and assembly

  • Component selection and BOM management

  • Experience in lightning and surge protection is a plus

Responsibilities:

  • PCB Layout & Routing - Perform or lead board placement and routing with attention to signal integrity, EMC, and power-path constraints.

  • Power & Thermal Architecture - Define and validate the power architecture of the product and the thermal strategy, including battery temperature management.

  • Environmental Robustness - Ensure the electronics withstand outdoor deployment conditions and define the associated qualification plan.

  • Component Selection & BOM Optimization - Select components with cost, availability, and reliability in mind; drive BOM cost reduction for mass production volumes.

  • Hardware Bring-up & Debug - Lead board bring-up, debug issues with oscilloscopes, power bench equipment, and other bench equipment; write bring-up scripts when needed.

  • EMC & Safety Compliance - Address EMC challenges; ensure signal integrity across the board and electrical safety of the power and battery sections.

  • Collaboration with Embedded SW - Work closely with the embedded software engineer to define hardware/software interfaces; support firmware bring-up.

  • Collaboration with Mechanical - Ensure seamless PCB integration into mechanical enclosures (connectors, mounting, thermal, sealing, shielding).

  • Supplier & Manufacturing Ramp-up - Qualify PCB manufacturers and assembly houses; support DFM/DFA review for production; manage NPI transitions.

  • Documentation - Maintain schematics, layout files, test procedures, and hardware specifications.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.
